BAY 1 and SFP+ 2 and 3 are physically present and identical - the cages are the same cages - but disabled by default and dust-capped, and unlocked by applying the A9K-9001-120G-LIC upgrade licence, after which the router must be reloaded. NOTE WHAT THIS CONFIGURATION STILL CANNOT SAY - see the config-scoped-device-attrs gap. It cannot mark SFP+ 2 and 3 as disabled, and it cannot carry the 60 Gbps figure, so both live in this sentence rather than in data.","kind":"model","part-numbers":{"ASR 9001-S Router with 2 x 10 GE":{"part":"ASR-9001-S"},"Upgrade license for 120G Bandwidth":{"part":"A9K-9001-120G-LIC"}}},"base":{"bays":{"mpa-0":"cisco/a9k-mpa-blank@1","mpa-1":"cisco/a9k-mpa-blank@1"},"default":true,"description":"Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 2 bay bays are EMPTY; cooling, power-modules are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.","kind":"base","source":"derived - built from the group roles rather than from a vendor bundle: every bay whose group is `service` or `management` keeps its seat, every `traffic` bay takes a blank. This vendor publishes no base configuration for this chassis, so the library defines one. Where a vendor DOES publish one, follow it instead and say so here."}},"description":"Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9001 Router - a 2 RU fixed-port aggregation services router with an integrated route processor, four fixed 10 GE SFP+ ports, two modular port adapter bays and 120 Gbps of fabric. Everything is on the front face: both MPA bays, both power supplies, the side-mounted fan tray and every port. The rear is a plain louvred panel.","format":1,"gaps":[{"blocks":[],"note":"HALF OF THIS IS FIXED. The ASR 9001-S's two licence-disabled SFP+ ports and its disabled modular bay are now stated: roc-ops/Portrayal#193 widened `component-attrs` to accept a placement id as well as a component name, and `bay-attrs` already took a bay path, so sfp-plus-2, sfp-plus-3 and mpa-1 carry `enabled: no` and the licence that unlocks them, in that configuration alone. WHAT IS STILL NOT SAYABLE is the 60 Gbps figure: a configuration can now say what is true of a PART and still cannot override an attr of the DEVICE, so this chassis carries the 120 Gbps switching capacity for both models and the -S's half-capacity lives in prose.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["asr-9001-s"],"wanted":"a way for a configuration to override a device-level attr - the same widening one level up. docs/what-a-configuration-cannot-say.md now records which two thirds of that shape are closed and why this one is not.","what":"config-scoped-device-attrs"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Table 4 of the fixed-port install guide gives the 10MHz and 1PPS connectors as DIN 1.0/2.3. The standards registry has no key for it - sma, smb, mcx and f-type are there, DIN 1.0/2.3 is not - so these two openings are declared as panel cutouts at their measured size rather than composed from a std/ part. Substituting sma or smb would name a connector Cisco does not. THE REASON WAS vendor-silent AND THAT WAS THE WRONG TOKEN. Cisco is not silent - it names the connector outright. What is missing is a panel-cutout dimension, which is needs-drawing, and the difference matters because the two tokens ask different things of a reader: vendor-silent reads as closed until better documents appear, needs-drawing reads as an errand somebody can run today. The correction came from asr9k-cards, who had just been wrong in exactly this direction about the XFP - concluding a figure was unsourceable after searching the intake rather than the standards - and found it in INF-8077i ten minutes after looking somewhere else. IEC 61169-8 is the somewhere else here, and nobody has opened it yet.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["clk-10mhz","clk-1pps"],"wanted":"a std/din-1-0-2-3 part and its standards.yaml key. THE CONNECTOR IS STANDARDISED, so a sourced dimension exists to be found rather than estimated - DIN 1.0/2.3 is specified in IEC 61169-8, and any manufacturer's bulkhead-jack panel drawing carries the D-hole figure. std/mcx is the worked example of exactly this being done properly earlier tonight: registered from IEC 61169-36 / CECC 22220 at 4.95 x 4.50 with confidence verified, replacing an estimate that was 28 percent too small. This should be done the same way, and until it is, an sma or smb standing in would be a plausible wrong answer - which is the failure mode this project keeps having to dig back out","what":"din-1-0-2-3-connector"}],"groups":{"cluster":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"cooling":{"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"Fan","role":"service","term":"Fan Tray"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":0,"mixed":"local and remote management access - console, auxiliary, Ethernet and USB","role":"management","term":"Port"},"mpa-bays":{"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"NetworkingDevice","role":"traffic","term":"Bay"},"power-modules":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 - two AC or two DC power modules for redundancy. The ASR 9001 FAQ states this directly; the 2+2 and 3+1 tables in the series install guide describe four-module chassis and do not apply to this two-bay one"},"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"PowerSupply","role":"service","term":"Power Supply"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"system-leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":0,"mixed":"the timing row - the ToD/1PPS jack and the two BITS/DTI SYNC jacks. One job (clock), two signal types on one 8P8C shell","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Cisco","maturity":"modelled","model":"ASR 9001","name":"asr-9001","portfolio":{"family":"Aggregation Services Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"ASR 9000 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"airflow":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the ASR 9001's fan tray runs along the router's right side and moves cool air through it from right to left, which is why the fan bay sits at the right end of the front face. The guide adds that 'Each power supply is also equipped with fans'"},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - the ASR 9001 data sheet's Table 2: 'Height: 3.472 inches (88.2 mm), Width: 17.42 inches (442 mm), Depth: 18.5 inches (470 mm), Weight of chassis: 30.2032 lbs (13.7 kg)'. THREE SOURCES AGREE ON THE HEIGHT to 0.06 percent - the data sheet's 3.472 in, the install guide's 'Cisco ASR 9901 Router and Cisco ASR 9001 Router is 3.47 inches (8.8 cm)', and the stencil master's props.height_in of 0.3472 at 1:10. So the rounding-up trap in stencil-as-metrology.md does not bite this chassis: 2 RU is 3.5 in and the chassis is built 0.028 in under it. chassis.width is the 442 BODY, not the 19 in rack face the stencil box carries"},"depth-axis-on-side-views":{"note":"THE FLANGE WAS AT THE WRONG END ON THREE OF THE FOUR SIDE VIEWS AND THE FIX IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. This is a front-mounted 2 RU chassis, so its integral flanges are at the FRONT - that half was never in doubt. What was in doubt was which end of each view the front is, because nothing in the schema, the renderer or any device file stated it, and this device answered it four different ways: top had the flange at y = 0, bottom at y = 464, left at x = 0 and right at x = 464. Four faces, one feature, three of them wrong, and no label anywhere to check the geometry against - which is why it survived. THE RENDERER IS THE AUTHORITY AND IT IS UNAMBIGUOUS. library/demo2/viewer3d.js builds each face in local coordinates (x right, y up, z out of the face) and orients it with a fixed rotation, with the front face at +z and the rear at -z. Applying those rotations to the local axes gives the depth direction of every side view outright: right is rot [0, +pi/2, 0], which sends local +x to world -z, so INCREASING x ON A RIGHT VIEW RUNS TOWARDS THE REAR AND x = 0 IS THE FRONT. left is rot [0, -pi/2, 0], which sends local +x to world +z, so x = 0 IS THE REAR AND x = depth IS THE FRONT. top is rot [-pi/2, 0, 0], which sends local +y to world -z; SVG y runs downwards so image y = 0 is local +y, giving y = 0 REAR and y = depth FRONT - the same answer Figure 9 gave for the ASR 9006 and 9904, now confirmed from the code as well as from the drawing. The box-UV path agrees independently, and so does viewer3d.js's own comment on the component branch, 'face end at image left -> front' for the right side. Three derivations, one answer. LEFT AND RIGHT ARE OPPOSITE AND THAT IS THE TRAP - they are two views of the same axis from opposite sides, so a feature at the front sits at x = 0 on one and x = depth on the other. Mirroring left from right by copying the x is exactly wrong, and copying it while ALSO negating it is exactly right. TOP AND BOTTOM ARE NOT OPPOSITE, which is the other half of the trap and the one that reads as inconsistent: looking at a chassis from below flips LEFT and RIGHT, not front and back, so top and bottom share a depth axis and a full-width strip has the SAME y on both"},"din-connectors":{"note":"THE 10MHz AND 1PPS PORTS ARE DECLARED AS PANEL CUTOUTS AND NOT COMPOSED, deliberately. Table 4 of the guide gives their connector as DIN 1.0/2.3, and there is no std/ part for it - the registry has sma, smb, mcx and f-type. Substituting one of those would name a connector Cisco does not. The holes are measured (about 4 mm, centred at y 68.0) and a gap records what is missing"},"face-check":{"note":"done BEFORE measuring, per the ASR 9910 lesson in stencil-as-metrology.md, where Cisco's master filenames name the wrong faces. No swap here: asr-9001-front carries the MPA bays, the PSU openings, every port, the LED cluster, the fan module and the 'Cisco ASR-9001' branding, and matches Figure 7 of the guide, 'Front Panel of the Cisco ASR 9001 Router'. asr-9001-rear is a plain louvred panel"},"fan-legend":{"note":"REMOVED, do not re-add at chassis level. \"ASR-9001 FAN\" and \"STATUS\" are printed on the FAN MODULE's own faceplate and cisco/asr-9001-fan already draws both inside its <g id=\"silkscreen\">. A chassis-level copy was both a duplicate and buried - it sat at (414.5, 84.0), inside the fan-0 bay, so the module painted over it. Text on a module's faceplate is that module's, not the chassis's"},"front-geometry":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured off the stencil master at the calibration above, expressed in body coordinates. The two MPA bays are one row at y 2.6 to 38.2, BAY 0 at x 20.0 to 182.9 and BAY 1 at x 208.9 to 371.9, each 163.0 wide and separated by a 26 mm divider that carries both captive screws and both BAY legends - which is what settles that the bays are SIDE BY SIDE and not stacked, since the two rotated legends sit at opposite ends of one divider. The PSU openings are at y 45.0 to 86.0, x 10.3 to 66.9 and 72.0 to 128.7, so 56.6 x 41.0 - against cisco/a9k-750w-ac's 55.2 x 39.9, agreeing to 2.5 percent, which is the confirmation that the data sheet's PSU PID is the part that fits"},"leds":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - eight discrete indicators, which matches the guide's callout 'Eight discrete LED indicators' on Figure 13. Grouped as the stencil draws them: RSP FAIL and LC FAIL in the left column, CRIT / MAJ / MIN in the middle, EUSB / ACO / SYNC on the right. Their POSITIONS are read off the master at a scale where the dots are a few pixels, so treat the grouping and the count as reliable and the millimetres as approximate"},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched and not found, with a caveat worth stating. No end-of-sale or end-of-life announcement for the ASR 9001 CHASSIS appears in the material held; the one EOL bulletin in the intake covers the ASR 9000 Series 4th Generation Ethernet Line Card Family, announced 2024-03-15, which is a different product. A live check was not possible - cisco.com returns 403 to this machine, which is why the whole intake came from the Wayback Machine - so this records 'nothing found in what we hold' rather than a confirmed absence"},"mpa-bays":{"note":"NOW BAYS - they were panel cutouts until cisco/a9k-mpa-blank@1 and cisco/a9k-mpa-20x1ge@1 landed, because device.schema.json requires accepts with minItems 1 and there was nothing legal to accept. The conversion was mechanical, as the placeholder note promised: the measurements did not move. THE BAYS ARE SIZED TO THE DRAWN OPENING, NOT TO THE MODULE, AND THAT IS WHY THEY SURVIVED THE MODULE CHANGING. I measured these openings at 163.0 x 35.6 off the front master. The module envelope they accept has since moved twice: first 33.81 x 160.02, read off the stencil shapesheet under the belief that no document dimensioned an MPA, and now 34.54 x 161.80 x 170.18 from Cisco data sheet c78-735809 Table 3, which lists every MPA by part number at 6.37 W x 1.36 H x 6.70 L and turns out to have been in the intake the whole time. A 5 percent change in the part, and nothing here needed editing, because a bay measured from the hole is not a restatement of the card. Had these bays been set to the shapesheet figure they would now be 0.73 and 1.78 mm UNDER the module they accept. Clearance against the sourced envelope is 1.20 along and 1.06 across - tighter than against the old figure and more plausible for a module in a bay. NOTE THE CORROBORATION THIS ENTRY USED TO CITE HAS BEEN RETRACTED. It claimed two independently derived figures agreeing, one of them the shapesheet reading, and that reading was wrong. The check is now stronger rather than weaker - a measured opening against a VENDOR-STATED envelope beats two derivations - but the sentence had to be rewritten, and a provenance entry citing a number that has since been withdrawn is exactly the stale-words failure this file spent the night finding in other people's files. THE OPENING DISAGREEMENT IS RESOLVED AND THE GEOMETRY DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE. asr9k-cards read these openings at 162.56 x 37.80 against my 163.0 x 35.6, and re-measured from scratch at an ear-inclusive 482.6 x 88.19 anchor that passes gate 1 on aspect to 0.7 percent, getting 163.66 x 37.79. WE WERE EACH RIGHT ON ONE AXIS: my along-card figure is 0.4 percent out against theirs at 0.7, and their across-card figure is the better one against my 5.8. THE REASON IS A PROPERTY OF THE STENCIL AND IS THE USEFUL PART. asr9k-cards measured this stencil against known standards across eight cards: ALONG-card readings carry a mean absolute error of 3.2 percent and always run slightly under, while ACROSS-card readings carry 14.7 percent with the sign scattering both ways - the same SFP opening is drawn at 8.96, 9.24, 10.72 and 12.04 mm on four different masters. IT IS A GOOD RULER ALONG A CARD AND A BAD ONE ACROSS IT, by a factor of four and a half. So a 6 percent disagreement across and 0.4 percent along is exactly what its accuracy predicts, and neither reading was careless. CITE THAT 14.7 PERCENT WITH ITS CAVEAT, WHICH asr9k-cards RAISED AGAINST THEIR OWN STUDY. All seven samples are apertures of essentially ONE SIZE, nominal 10.00 to 10.15 mm. Their absolute errors spread 0.72 to 2.06 mm and their percentage errors spread 7.2 to 20.4 - the same 2.9-fold scatter expressed two ways - so with no size leverage in the sample there is no way to tell whether the error SCALES with the feature or is a fixed drawing tolerance. The honest quotation is '14.7 percent mean, measured on ~10 mm apertures', and it must not be carried onto a 37 mm opening in either direction: not as 14.7 percent, which may be far too harsh, and not as the ~4 percent a fixed-tolerance reading would imply, which is unsupported. An earlier version of this entry quoted the bare 14.7 as though it transferred, and it does not. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES THE CAVEAT, which is why nothing moved. The two readings differ by 2.19 mm. On the characterisation LEAST favourable to my figure - a fixed absolute tolerance, mean around 1.5 mm - that gap is still about 1.5 times what this instrument has demonstrated it can be wrong by, so the disagreement is inside its known failure range either way. The decision rests on the data as it is, not on the harshest reading of it. WHICH IS ALSO WHY 37.79 IS NOT ADOPTED. That figure sits on the axis their own study says is unreliable, so it is not a better number than 35.6 - it is a differently-placed sample from a ruler with 14.7 percent scatter, and both readings are inside that noise. Taking their along-card figure and keeping mine across would be cherry-picking two measurements by axis; taking the pair whole would move a working number onto the bad axis for no gain. THE BAY IS INSIDE THE HOLE ON EITHER READING AND OUTSIDE NOTHING ELSE, which is all a bay has to be: it clears the 34.54 module by 1.06 across, and the true opening on either reading swallows the bay. If a caliper ever settles the across-card axis, 163.66 x 37.79 is the candidate to adopt WHOLE, and this is the note that says so. The bays carry rotate 90 because the modules are drawn portrait and this chassis lays them flat; the bay size is the ROTATED footprint, which is the convention asr9k-cards verified with a scratch device rather than asserted. WIDENED after the XFP MPAs landed: both bays now accept 20x1ge, 2x10ge, 4x10ge and the blank. All four share the 33.81 x 160.02 envelope, so widening accepts needed no geometry change - which is the point of an envelope shared across a family. COMPLETE, AND THE LIST IS THE CHASSIS'S OWN. a9k-mpa-1x40ge landed and both bays now accept all four adapters plus the blank. THE ELIGIBILITY IS NOT INFERRED FROM THE FAMILY: the fixed-port install guide has a section headed 'Modular Port Adapters' that says outright 'The Cisco ASR 9001 Router has two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)' and then lists exactly four - 20-Port Gigabit Ethernet, 4-Port 10 Gigabit Ethernet, 2-Port 10 Gigabit Ethernet and 1-Port 40 Gigabit Ethernet. That is a per-CHASSIS list rather than a per-family one, which is the distinction that decides what belongs here. A9K-MPA-2X40GE AND A9K-MPA-8X10GE ARE MODELLED IN THE LIBRARY AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ACCEPTED: a list that names four is excluding the others, and a card existing on the same 33.81 x 160.02 envelope says it would FIT, not that it is SUPPORTED. READ THE LIST IN THE PDF AND NOT IN THE TEXT DUMP - the fourth bullet is separated from the first three by a page break, so the extracted text puts a running header, a page number and a section title between them and a reader scanning the bulleted block finds only three. ONE WARNING FOR ANYONE TOUCHING THE 40GE ARTWORK: its stencil master prints BOTH 'A9K-MPA-1X40GE' AND 'A9K-MPA-2X10GE' on the same faceplate, so the artwork is shared and the silkscreen legend cannot be used to tell the two apart"},"port-cutouts":{"note":"DERIVED, not measured, and the distinction matters. Every one of the fifteen front ports conforms to a registry standard - `rj45-ganged` 12.7 x 11.0, `sfp-ganged` 14.25 x 10.4, `usb-a` 12.0 x 4.5 - and a standard connector's bezel opening IS its aperture at its position. There was nothing independent to measure: the hole is implied by \"there is an SFP cage here\", and the only sourced fact is where the cage is, which the placements already carried. SO THE CHECKS THAT PASS HERE ARE CIRCULAR AND SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY. L39 compares each hole against the standard its occupant conforms to, and against where that occupant lands; both were used to generate it, so both confirm the arithmetic rather than the model. What they do catch from here on is DRIFT - a port moved without its hole, or a hole resized against its standard. THEY ARE NOT GANGED, which was checked rather than assumed. SFF-8433 gives a 1xN SFP+ assembly ONE continuous opening at N x 14.25 + 1.2, and rj45-ganged abuts on a 13.97 pitch. This panel's columns sit 20.5 to 47.6 apart, so no two of these ports share a cutout and fifteen separate holes is right. THE USB IS THE ONE THAT NEEDED THINKING ABOUT. It is placed `rotate: 90`, and `rotate` pivots a part on its own pre-rotation centre, so the hole is the LANDED box - (274.25, 58.95) at 4.5 x 12 - not the placement's `at` with the standard's unrotated size. Deriving it the naive way put the hole 3.75mm off, which is (12.0 - 4.5) / 2 and exactly the error L39 gained a check for in #32. The rule caught it on the first run."},"port-rows":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - every stacked port pair sits on the SAME two rows, which is what makes the reading safe: the upper row at y 46.5 to 55.4 and the lower at 62.6 to 71.4, a 16.1 mm pitch, reproduced independently at eight different x positions. The SFP cages measure a 15.3 mm belly-to-belly pitch against the 15.00 std/sfp-ganged carries from a measured TE part"},"port-speeds":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"the fixed-port install guide, Table 4 (front panel ports, shared with the 9901): SVC LAN is a 10/100 Mb/s Ethernet port for an IEEE 1588 grandmaster, so `100m`; MGT LAN 0 and 1 are tri-speed 10/100/1000, so `1g`. The data sheet (c78-685687) gives the two CLUSTER ports as 10 G out-of-band Ethernet ports for nV clustering, so the group is `10g` and `sfp-plus` - Table 4 calls the cage SFP and says it takes copper or optical modules, and a 10G module in an SFP cage is SFP+. The same table types the rest by what they carry, not by a rate: TOD is time of day with 1PPS over RS-422 (`rj45-tod`), SYNC 0/1 are BITS or DTI (`rj48`), CONSOLE and AUX are RS-232 (`rj45-serial`)."},"rear":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the rear is a plain louvred panel and that is the finding, not an omission. Horizontal vent slots across the full width, six screws and the two rack ears. No connectors and no modules: on this chassis the PSUs, the fan tray, both MPA bays and every port are on the FRONT"},"sfp-plus-numbering":{"note":"READ AT HIGH ZOOM, AND DO NOT 'FIX' IT. The left cage is SFP+ 3 over SFP+ 1 and the right cage is SFP+ 2 over SFP+ 0, so numbering runs RIGHT TO LEFT along the bottom row and then right to left along the top: port 0 bottom-right, 1 bottom-left, 2 top-right, 3 top-left. This looks like a transcription error and is not one - it is what the stencil prints and what the guide's Figure 13 shows. It is the same class of trap as the rotated crop that once reversed an entire supervisor card in this project: the obvious reading is wrong and looks right. If a future reader is tempted to renumber these left-to-right, the thing to do is re-read the artwork at 4x, not the manifest"},"side-faces":{"note":"no figure in either document shows the top, bottom or side faces of this chassis, so they are sized from the data sheet and carry only the integral rack flanges. Stated rather than left blank, as on the Casa chassis"},"sources":{"note":"the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide (b-asr9001-hardware-installation-guide.pdf, retitled from the ASR 9001 HIG and now covering the 9001, 9901, 9902 and 9903); the Cisco ASR 9001 Router Data Sheet (c78-685687); and Cisco's own Visio stencil Routers-Cisco_ASR_9000_11_15_13, masters asr-9001-front and asr-9001-rear"},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 3 SFP pairs (cluster-1/cluster-0 to sfp-plus-2/sfp-plus-0)."},"stencil-calibration":{"note":"the asr-9001-front master calibrates to 0.66 percent between its two axes - x on the 19.0 in rack face (0.18562 mm/px over 2600 px) and y on the data sheet's 88.2 mm (0.18452 mm/px over 478 px). By stencil-as-metrology.md that is trustworthy but not pristine; the ASR 9904 managed 0.06 percent. CONFIRMED ON SOMETHING NEVER USED AS AN INPUT: with x calibrated on the rack face, the body's left edge measures 21.0 mm, against 20.3 mm predicted by (482.6 - 442) / 2 from two data sheet numbers. That is the note's third check and it passes"},"variants":{"note":"the ASR 9001-S is a CONFIGURATION, not a second device, because the rule in portfolio-taxonomy-design.md is that a new device.yaml is warranted only when the sheet metal differs. It does not here: same chassis, same faceplate, same four cages, with two ports and one bay disabled in software until A9K-9001-120G-LIC is applied. The stencil having its own asr-9001-s-front master is not evidence to the contrary - a marketing stencil drawing a variant separately says nothing about the metal. What the configuration cannot express is recorded in the config-scoped-device-attrs gap"}},"references":[{"sha256":"8b539355306e5bd2cfd9293a07dfe3acc95cb6aa95435537225b667901ac9d13","title":"Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide
